descriptionChirho: The physical organ of hearing, used both literally (the bodily ear) and in figurative expressions about spiritual receptivity ('he who has ears, let him hear'). All 37 occurrences denote the same anatomical referent with variation limited to grammatical number (singular 'ear' vs. plural 'ears') and case. Multilingual evidence: spa 'oído/oídos/oreja' (ear/ears, inner and outer), hin 'कान/कानों' (kān/kānon, ear/ears), arb 'أُذُنٌ/آذَانِ' ('udhun/ādhān, ear sg/pl from same root أ-ذ-ن), kor '귀/귀를/귀로' (gwi, ear in various particles), swa 'sikio/masikio' (ear sg class 5/pl class 6, standard Bantu number pairing). Used in Matt 10:27, 11:15, 13:9, Mark 4:9, Luke 4:21, Acts 7:57, Rev 2:7 etc.
